verses.text: Here is the count of the Israelites who served the king: family heads, commanders of thousands and hundreds, and their officers. Their divisions rotated in and out of service each month throughout the year, with twenty-four thousand in each division.
Jashobeam son of Zabdiel led the first division, which served in the first month and numbered twenty-four thousand.
He descended from Perez and was in charge of all the army commanders for the first month.
Dodai the Ahohite led the division for the second month, with Mikloth as its officer. His division numbered twenty-four thousand.
Benaiah son of Jehoiada the chief priest was the third army commander, serving in the third month. His division numbered twenty-four thousand.
This was the Benaiah who was a mighty warrior among the Thirty and led them. His son Ammizabad served with his division.
Asahel, Joab's brother, commanded the fourth division in the fourth month, and his son Zebadiah succeeded him. His division numbered twenty-four thousand.
Shamhuth the Izrahite commanded the fifth division in the fifth month. His division numbered twenty-four thousand.
Ira son of Ikkesh the Tekoite commanded the sixth division in the sixth month. His division numbered twenty-four thousand.
Helez the Pelonite, from Ephraim, commanded the seventh division in the seventh month. His division numbered twenty-four thousand.
Sibbecai the Hushathite, from the Zerahites, commanded the eighth division in the eighth month. His division numbered twenty-four thousand.
Abiezer the Anathothite, from Benjamin, commanded the ninth division in the ninth month. His division numbered twenty-four thousand.
Maharai the Netophathite, from the Zerahites, commanded the tenth division in the tenth month. His division numbered twenty-four thousand.
Benaiah the Pirathonite, from Ephraim, commanded the eleventh division in the eleventh month. His division numbered twenty-four thousand.
Heldai the Netophathite, from Othniel's family, commanded the twelfth division in the twelfth month. His division numbered twenty-four thousand.
These were the leaders of Israel's tribes: Eliezer son of Zichri led Reuben, and Shephatiah son of Maacah led Simeon.
Hashabiah son of Kemuel led Levi, and Zadok led Aaron's family.
Elihu, one of David's brothers, led Judah, and Omri son of Michael led Issachar.
Ishmaiah son of Obadiah led Zebulun, and Jeremoth son of Azriel led Naphtali.
Hoshea son of Azaziah led Ephraim, and Joel son of Pedaiah led half the tribe of Manasseh.
Iddo son of Zechariah led the half-tribe of Manasseh in Gilead, and Jaasiel son of Abner led Benjamin.
Azarel son of Jeroham led Dan. These were the leaders of Israel's tribes.
David left those twenty years old and younger out of the count, because the LORD had promised to make Israel as numerous as the stars in the sky.
Joab son of Zeruiah started counting the people but never finished. Wrath came on Israel because of this, and the count was left out of King David's official records.
Azmaveth son of Adiel managed the king's treasuries. Jonathan son of Uzziah managed the stores in the countryside, cities, villages, and towers.
Ezri son of Chelub supervised the workers who cultivated the fields.
Shimei the Ramathite oversaw the vineyards, and Zabdi the Shiphmite managed the wine going into the cellars.
Baal Hanan the Gederite oversaw the olive and sycamore trees in the lowlands, and Joash managed the oil stores.
Shitrai the Sharonite oversaw the herds grazing in Sharon, and Shaphat son of Adlai oversaw the herds in the valleys.
Obil the Ishmaelite managed the camels. Jehdeiah the Meronothite managed the donkeys. Jaziz the Hagrite managed the flocks.
These were the people in charge of King David's property.
David's uncle Jonathan was an adviser, a man of good judgment, and a scribe. Jehiel son of Hachmoni attended the king's sons.
Ahithophel was the king's adviser, and Hushai the Archite was the king's friend.
Jehoiada son of Benaiah and Abiathar came after Ahithophel. Joab commanded the king's army.
